discovery: Foundations of the statistical physics of active matter: flocking transitions and the hydrodynamic theory of self-propelled systems

nominees.name: Sriram Ramaswamy
nominees.affiliation: Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore, India

motivation: In 1995 Vicsek introduced a minimal model of self-propelled particles showing that local alignment alone produces a phase transition to collective motion. Toner (with Yuhai Tu) built the hydrodynamic field theory of flocks, proving that true long-range orientational order exists in two dimensions, which equilibrium systems forbid (Mermin-Wagner), and predicting giant number fluctuations. Ramaswamy extended continuum theory to active suspensions and active nematics, showing the generic instability of ordered active fluids. Together they founded a new branch of non-equilibrium statistical mechanics: matter whose constituents consume energy locally. Their concepts now organise quantitative experiments on bacterial swarms, cytoskeletal extracts, epithelial tissues, colloidal rollers and bird flocks, and they connect physics with biology and materials science. Starting from simple microscopic rules, this work gives a clear coarse-grained picture of a messy many-body problem, and it has changed how physicists think about phases far from equilibrium.
